BiblicalUsage: Sethav is winter, the dark rainy season, and it appears once, in the Song — the winter is past, the rain is over and gone, and the time of singing has come.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe winter in Scripture is never the end of the story; it is the season before the singing.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
